title: CRS-Triage: Confidence- and Reliability-Aware Selective Triage under Incomplete Clinical Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2608.03862v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Emergency triage requires reliable decisions within a short time period. However, the available electronic health record (EHR) data, including structured data and clinical text, are often incomplete, unreliable, and inconsistent. This makes machine learning (ML)-based triage prediction more challenging, as existing ML models typically rely on complete and reliable EHR data to accurately predict patients' acuity levels. To address this, we propose confidence- and reliability-aware selective triage (CRS-Triage) to predict patients' acuity levels with a confidence score. By comparing the confidence score with a predefined threshold, CRS-Triage can selectively determine whether the model should make the decision or defer the case. translated_title: CRS-Triage：在不完整临床证据下基于置信度与可靠性感知的选择性分诊
translated_abstract: 急诊分诊需要在短时间内做出可靠的决策。然而，可用的电子健康记录（EHR）数据，包括结构化数据和临床文本，往往是不完整、不可靠且不一致的。这使得基于机器学习（ML）的分诊预测更具挑战性，因为现有的机器学习模型通常依赖完整且可靠的EHR数据来准确预测患者的病情严重程度。为解决这一问题，我们提出了置信度与可靠性感知的选择性分诊方法（CRS-Triage），以带置信度分数的方式预测患者的病情严重程度。通过将置信度分数与预定义阈值进行比较，CRS-Triage可以选择性地决定模型是应该做出决策还是推迟处理该病例。具体而言，CRS-Triage分别评估结构化数据和临床文本的可靠性，然后联合考虑两种模态之间的一致性来估计每个预测的置信度。
tldr: 该论文提出CRS-Triage方法，通过分别评估结构化数据与临床文本的可靠性并综合考虑两者的一致性来生成置信度分数，使分诊模型能够在不完整临床证据下选择性地做出预测或推迟决策。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes CRS-Triage, which generates confidence scores by separately evaluating the reliability of structured data and clinical text and jointly considering their consistency, enabling the triage model to selectively make predictions or defer decisions under incomplete clinical evidence.
